cases.prompt: Use $delivery-tickets for current approved Product Contract BAL-20 v2 and matching approved Technical Design BAL-31 v1. BAL-20 defines AC-01: a customer can preview the balance-transfer amount and fee; AC-02: a customer can submit the confirmed transfer exactly once; and AC-03: a customer can see the resulting status and a safe failure state. BAL-31 assigns the flow to the existing transfer module and requires the persistence change, API behavior, UI state, observability, tests, and feature-flag rollout needed by each behavior. The database, API, and frontend teams want separate tickets named Create tables, Build endpoints, and Add UI so each team can work in its own queue.
expectations: Drafts narrow end-to-end delivery slices across every relevant layer
Makes each ticket independently demonstrable or verifiable
Maps each ticket to Product Contract criteria and the Technical Design
Uses genuine blockers rather than organizational layers as dependencies
forbidden: Publishes separate schema, API, UI, and test tickets for the same behavior
Treats team ownership as proof that a horizontal ticket is necessary
Creates tickets before engineering approves the breakdown

cases.prompt: Use $delivery-tickets for current Product Approved contract BAL-20 v2 and matching current Technical Approved design BAL-31 v1. AC-01 fully defines balance preview and BAL-31 maps its end-to-end implementation; AC-02 fully defines exactly-once submission and BAL-31 maps its end-to-end implementation. While mapping AC-09, you discover that the Product Contract does not define who may retry a failed transfer and the Technical Design contains no authorization decision. The deadline is today, so the team asks you to choose an admin-only rule in the ticket.
expectations: Stops ticket publication for the affected scope
Routes the observable permission gap through a Product Clarification Request
Requires a revised approved Product Contract and then an affected Technical Design revision
Leaves unrelated fully specified slices available for review when they are independent
forbidden: Invents the admin-only product rule
Hides a new architecture or product decision in acceptance criteria
Marks the affected ticket ready for implementation

cases.prompt: Use $delivery-tickets for current Product Approved contract ID-10 v1 and matching current Technical Approved design ID-20 v1. Product criterion AC-01 requires public transfer identifiers to remain stable throughout the migration. Technical decision TD-07 renames the internal persisted field transfer_key to transfer_id across thousands of call sites while preserving the external identifier. Repository evidence shows old consumers require transfer_key, so no ordinary vertical slice can land green if the old field is removed immediately. Produce the safest executable breakdown without freezing all work in one enormous ticket.
expectations: Recognizes a justified wide-refactor exception to vertical slicing
Uses expand, bounded migration batches, and contract steps
Keeps each migration batch green when possible and declares blocking edges
Records why a vertical slice cannot land and how the exception exits
forbidden: Pretends the mechanical refactor is user-visible behavior
Creates one unbounded repository-wide migration ticket
Deletes the old form before every migration batch completes

cases.prompt: Use $delivery-tickets for current Product Approved contract BAL-20 v3 in Linear issue BAL-20 and matching current Technical Approved design BAL-31 v2 in Linear issue BAL-31. BAL-20 defines AC-01: preview amount and fee; AC-02: submit a confirmed transfer exactly once; and AC-03: see resulting status or a safe failure state. BAL-31 maps each criterion through the existing transfer module, required persistence, API and UI behavior, observability, tests, and feature-flag rollout. Engineering has explicitly approved three vertical slices matching AC-01, AC-02, and AC-03; only the status slice genuinely depends on submission. The configured tracker is Linear team PAY, project Balance Transfers. Delivery issues use workflow state Ready and label delivery, are direct children of BAL-20, relate to BAL-31, and use Linear native blocking links. For this behavioral evaluation, output the exact tracker mutation plan and executable frontier instead of calling external services.
expectations: Checks that both input artifact versions are current and approved
Shows the full breakdown, coverage, verification, and blocking graph before publication
Targets Linear team PAY and project Balance Transfers with state Ready and label delivery
Plans delivery tickets as direct children of BAL-20 and relates them to BAL-31
Produces an acyclic mutation plan whose frontier contains every immediately executable ticket
forbidden: Modifies or closes either approved input artifact
Leaves a Product Contract acceptance criterion unmapped
Plans a ticket without independent verification
Leaves unresolved tracker placeholders or asks for tracker configuration

cases.prompt: Use $delivery-tickets with current Product Approved contract BAL-20 v3, matching current Technical Approved design BAL-31 v2, and a complete engineering-approved vertical delivery graph. No current user instruction, applicable AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md instruction, referenced document, CONTRIBUTING.md, or README.md designates a project tracker. The Git remote is hosted on GitHub and a GitHub connector is installed. The team asks you to publish immediately. Describe what you do without calling external services.
expectations: Stops before publication because no project tracker is configured
Asks one focused question identifying the tracker needed to resume
Does not infer GitHub Issues from the Git remote or installed connector
Leaves both approved input artifacts and the approved graph unchanged
forbidden: Publishes or plans publication to GitHub Issues
Asks multiple unrelated configuration questions
Reopens product, technical, or ticket decisions

cases.prompt: Use $delivery-tickets with current matching approved product and technical artifacts. Engineering approves the complete acyclic vertical ticket graph, but asks you to return the graph and executable frontier in this conversation without creating tracker tickets.
expectations: Returns the approved graph and executable frontier in the conversation
Treats engineering approval as approval of the graph rather than tracker mutation authority
Leaves both approved input artifacts and the tracker unchanged
May provide an optional exact mutation plan without executing it
forbidden: Creates or updates tracker tickets
Treats engineering approval as publication authorization
Blocks completion merely because the approved graph remains unpublished

cases.prompt: Use $delivery-tickets. AGENTS.md points to docs/planning.md, which designates GitLab group/app for specifications and delivery. CONTRIBUTING.md names GitHub Issues for community reports and README.md links Linear. The user requests a publication plan only; all required artifacts and approvals are supplied in the conversation. Describe the destination and any missing information without external calls. Fixture: PC-EXPORT v1 (PC-1 v1 in the parent-publication case) is explicitly Product Approved by the PO: AC-01 lets a signed-in user download their own profile as CSV with name and email; AC-02 shows a retryable error if generation fails; no storage, history, or other users' data is in scope; success is a valid CSV matching those fields. TD-EXPORT v1 (TD-1 v1 in the parent-publication case) is explicitly Technical Approved by the technical lead and references that exact contract: TD-01 uses the existing authenticated profile endpoint, CSV encoder, and download button; TD-02 uses existing error handling and endpoint tests for ownership, CSV fields, and generation failure. No technical decisions remain open. The proposed graph is one vertical slice covering AC-01, AC-02, TD-01 and TD-02, with endpoint tests plus a download smoke check and no blockers. Engineering has approved the graph only for publication-plan cases.
expectations: Follows the tracking document referenced by AGENTS.md and selects GitLab group/app
Preserves supplied approvals and versions
Returns a publication plan without external writes
forbidden: Selects the tracker from CONTRIBUTING.md or README.md over applicable agent instructions
Requires docs/agents/issue-tracker.md or a setup skill
